author: Temminck & Schlegel), 1848

art.subject: Japanese Accentor (Prunella rubida), adult (sexes alike), a winter vagrant in Korean forest undergrowth: crown and nape warm dark brown; face, throat and breast slate-grey, the ear coverts brownish with fine pale flecks; mantle and scapulars rufous-brown with heavy blackish streaks; wings rufous-brown with dark centres to the coverts and tertials; flanks brown with dark streaks; belly paler grey; tail plain dark brown. Bill thin, pointed and blackish; eye dark; legs pinkish-brown.
art.pose: creeping on leaf litter at the edge of a thicket, side view
art.scene: leaf litter beneath dwarf bamboo and shrubs at the edge of a Korean mountain forest in winter (January), cold soft light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Small and sparrow-sized but slimmer, with a rounded head, short neck and low, horizontal posture; shuffles mouse-like on the ground under cover. Bill thin and pointed like a warbler's, much shorter than the head, not conical. Legs medium length, pinkish-brown. Wings short and rounded, the wingtips reaching just past the base of the tail. Tail medium length and square, plain dark brown with no white.
avoid: Do not paint a thick, conical seed-eater bill; accentors have a thin, pointed bill.
Do not paint a bold buff supercilium or a black crown and ear patch — that is Siberian Accentor, the accentor usually seen in Korea.
Do not paint wing bars or white tail sides.
Do not paint a sparrow-like black bib.
